# City Safety Map

> Free, open-source city crime and safety maps built on real police incident
> reports. No ads, no tracking, no accounts.
> San Francisco: https://citysafetymap.com/sf/ (refreshed nightly)
> New York City: https://citysafetymap.com/nyc/ (NYPD publishes quarterly)

Source code: https://github.com/ZihuiTommyWang/sf-safety-map

## San Francisco (citysafetymap.com/sf)

- Data source: San Francisco Police Department incident reports, via DataSF's
  public dataset "Police Department Incident Reports: 2018 to Present"
  (https://data.sf.gov/d/wg3w-h783). Refreshed nightly.
- Coverage: the most recent 3 years (~150,000+ incidents); the map defaults to
  showing the most recent year.
- Only place-based safety incidents are shown. Administrative records (warrants,
  lost property, traffic stops), fraud, shoplifting, and other non-place-based
  reports are filtered out. Incidents are grouped into 13 categories such as
  Assault, Robbery, Theft, Car Break-In & Damage, Burglary, Drugs, and Street
  Disorder.
- Every dot on the map is one real incident report — nothing is smoothed or
  interpolated. Searching an address shows the incident count within 300 m
  compared to a typical SF location, plus the most recent reports.
- Address search covers every official San Francisco address (from the city's
  Enterprise Addressing System) plus places via OpenStreetMap.

## New York City (citysafetymap.com/nyc)

- Data sources: New York Police Department complaint reports, via NYC Open
  Data's "NYPD Complaint Data Historic" (https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/qgea-i56i)
  and "NYPD Complaint Data Current (Year To Date)"
  (https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/5uac-w243). The NYPD publishes this data
  quarterly, so the map lags the calendar by up to a few months; the About
  panel shows the exact date the data runs through.
- Coverage: the most recent 3 years (~1,000,000 incidents); the map defaults
  to showing the most recent year.
- Same filtering philosophy as San Francisco, adapted to NYPD's taxonomy: the
  largest exclusions are Harassment (interpersonal texts/calls/disputes),
  Theft of Services (fare evasion), traffic enforcement, fraud, and
  shoplifting. The same 13 categories are used.
- Address search covers every official NYC address (from the city's Address
  Point registry, including Queens hyphenated numbers) plus places via
  OpenStreetMap.

## Caveats

- Reported incidents are not a perfect measure of risk: report density also
  reflects police presence, foot traffic, and reporting habits.
- SFPD and NYPD anonymize incident locations to the block or intersection level.

## Data files

- Incidents (columnar JSON): https://citysafetymap.com/sf/data/incidents.json
- Metadata and category definitions: https://citysafetymap.com/sf/data/meta.json
